es.title: Articles, identity and location
es.note: El and la mark singular noun gender: el libro, la casa. Soy is the yo form of ser for identity; estoy is the yo form of estar for location. Hablo is the yo present form of hablar. Adjectives may agree in gender: la casa blanca. Spanish ñ is a separate letter, and ¿ opens a question. Missing accents may be accepted when typing, but read and learn the written accents shown in the examples.

it.title: Articles, agreement and everyday verbs
it.note: Il libro is masculine and la casa feminine. Lo is used before s plus a consonant, as in lo studente; l' is used before a vowel, as in l'amica. Sono is the io form of essere. Parlo is the io present form of parlare. An adjective agrees with its noun: la casa bianca. È means is; e means and. Learn accented forms even when the keyboard-friendly scoring accepts plain vowels.

de.title: Articles, word order and cases
de.note: Learn nouns with their articles: der Mann, die Frau, das Buch. German nouns begin with a capital. In a statement the finite verb takes the second position: Heute lerne ich Deutsch. A direct masculine object changes der to den: Ich sehe den Mann. After mit use dative: mit dem Mann. Ä, ö and ü have umlauts; ß is a separate spelling character. Keyboard-friendly answers may accept plain Latin forms, but the written model remains standard German.

ru.title: Cyrillic, gender and first cases
ru.note: Russian uses Cyrillic; do not replace Russian letters with similar-looking Latin letters. Книга is feminine and стол masculine; окно is neuter. There are no articles. The present-tense equivalent of am/is/are is normally omitted: Я студент. Учить changes to учу after я. Compare nominative книга, accusative книгу, genitive книги and prepositional книге in the examples. Ь and ъ are signs, not independent vowel sounds. Ё and е remain distinct in Russian grading.
